I added `GET /api/admin/users/recently-created`. I didn't run the build or any tests, as you asked, so none of this has been compiled or exercised.

- **Repository** (`UserRepository`): `findLoginsByCreatedDateAfter(Instant since, Pageable)` is a JPQL query that selects `u.login` where `createdDate >= :since`. The caller passes in the date boundary.
- **Service** (`UserService`): `getRecentlyCreatedLogins(Pageable)` is read-only and computes `Instant.now(clock).minus(7, DAYS)`. The service now takes a `java.time.Clock` in its constructor, because `docs/backend.md` requires that instead of calling `now()` directly.
- **Clock bean**: the project had no `Clock` bean, so I added `config/ClockConfiguration.java` with `Clock.systemUTC()`. No test builds `UserService` by hand, so the new constructor argument shouldn't break any.
- **Resource** (`UserResource`): the endpoint carries `@PreAuthorize` with `AuthoritiesConstants.ADMIN`, and it sits under `/api/admin`, which the URL rules already restrict to admins. It uses the same sort allow-list as `GET /api/admin/users`. The fixed path takes precedence over `/users/{login}`.

The endpoint is paged (default 20 logins per page, with pagination headers) rather than returning every login. `docs/backend.md` forbids unbounded lists from REST endpoints. If you want a plain unpaged list, tell me and I'll change it.

I didn't add tests or update `notes/`, which doesn't exist in this project.
